title: How much do you trust your agents to trade?
author: One_Commission_6986
selftext:
I've got good experience in Claude Code generally, and use multiple automations to make my life and job easier - and now I'm trying to use that knowledge for agentic investing. 

I'm initially interested in basic set ups, e.g. BTC DCA, or buying when crossing above the moving average and selling when moving below - and weirdly I never have seem to have enough time to do this stuff manually, but will commit way more time to try and automate it.

Given what I know about LLMs, and that even if you include something in [claude.md](http://claude.md), and explicit do/don't rules in skills, hooks, agents, etc - they still sometimes do what you say not to do. 

All these threads are full of people saying that AIs will go rogue and do things you don't want, e.g. ape into 100x leverage and lose all your money, but has anyone actually seen this happen?

I've seen some protocols offer sandboxing to reduce the risk from this, but that will always limit how much you can trade. So are there any better guardrails / protection systems out there?

comments.author: jaw_line
comments.body: Ai discernment will only troll you when trading as of now
